notes:
## Fix
- Fixed recomps failing to launch with "spawn EPERM" and seeming to vanish from their folder. A folder-lock added in a recent update could deny the game's own process access on Windows. Hanami no longer changes Windows file permissions, and it automatically repairs any install the old lock affected — your recomps should open normally again (Neon Coast stays on 🌴).

## 🌴 Neon Coast — a limited-time makeover
- To celebrate a certain long-awaited trip to the sunny coast, Hanami is wearing a neon Vice-City sunset for the week — palms, synthwave sun and all
- The whole launcher and the in-game overlay get the treatment: hot pink, cyan and sunset gradients
- It switches itself back to normal automatically after about a week — no action needed
- Not feeling it? Settings › 🌴 Neon Coast toggles it off (or back on) any time while it lasts

## Encrypting your recomps
- Encrypted recomp packages: the download itself is scrambled, so grabbing it off GitHub or a mirror gives junk — you need Hanami to open it
- Installed code and assets are encrypted at rest and bound to your PC, so a copied folder, backup or synced copy is dead weight anywhere else
- The files are unlocked into place only while you're actually playing ("Preparing to play…"), then wiped the moment you close the game
- Your saves, your online account and the game data are left alone — only your code and assets get sealed
- Plain, unencrypted recomps keep working exactly as before

## Protecting your recomps
- Recomps now install into a hidden, permission-locked folder instead of a browsable one — other accounts on the PC can't wander in
- The downloaded copy is deleted after install, and debug symbols, source and build leftovers are stripped out, so there's nothing lying around to copy or poke at
- Already-installed recomps get locked automatically too, the next time Hanami starts
- The game's own files and your saves are untouched — this only hides the parts a code-thief would go for

- The in-game Home menu uses a game screenshot behind Now Playing when a game's banner art is just a plain backdrop (like Demon Slayer 2's)
- The achievement ring's glow no longer shows as a square, especially on platinums

## Recomps
- When a recomp has a new version, Play becomes Update! — updates are required before you can play, since some fix essential things
- Move a recomp to another drive from the ••• menu — Hanami copies it, checks every file, then frees up the old drive
## Steam games
- The trash can on Steam games now uninstalls the game for you — no more trips to Steam
- Steam's "Starting game" popup no longer shows when you press Play
## In-game Home menu
- A brand-new Home menu: a Now Playing card with your session timer and total playtime, your friends, messages and downloads alongside, and a quick-action dock
- See your achievement progress for the game you're playing — gamerscore, what to go for next and this session's unlocks
- Open the full achievement list without leaving your game

Levels show automatically, like Xbox ✿
• Your level and gamerscore now show to friends automatically. Hanami links with Steam quietly in the background, using the Steam sign-in it already has
• If Steam ever needs you to sign in first, your profile shows a Finish linking with Steam card
• Don't want it? Settings → Achievements → Show my level and gamerscore to friends (turning it off deletes it from the server)
• Fixed: linking with Steam was blocked by Steam's servers (needs the WFC server update too)

Small fix ✿
• A friend's profile now tells you when they haven't shared their Hanami level yet, instead of quietly showing only their Steam level

Achievement popups ✿
• Hanami now has its own Xbox-style achievement popup, with the gamerscore you just earned, and a special one with a petal burst when you get a platinum
• While Hanami is open, Steam's own popups and sounds stay quiet, so you only see Hanami's. Your Steam settings come back exactly as they were when Hanami closes
• Choose in Settings → Achievements: all of Steam's popups off, just achievement popups off, or leave Steam alone. There's a Preview button too
• Steam games: popups appear the moment you unlock something. This uses Hanami's Steam connection (Settings → Silent installs)
• War for Cybertron: popups come from Hanami once WFC updates to 1.0.1, which turns the game's own popup off when Hanami launches it

Achievements with gamerscore ✿
• Trophies are now Xbox-style achievements: every achievement is worth gamerscore, and your profile shows your total G
• Platinums stay: 100% a game and it still gets its platinum, which also boosts your level
• Your level stays too, now built from your gamerscore plus your platinums
• WFC uses its real Xbox 360 gamerscore (1000G). Steam games get up to 1000G each, shared out by rarity, so rarer achievements are worth more; once given, the values stay put
• Friends: their level and gamerscore show in your friends list and on their profile

Friends' WFC trophies for everyone ✿
• You don't need War for Cybertron installed to see a friend's WFC trophies anymore: the full list, descriptions and real icons come from the Hanami Store
• Their recent WFC trophies show their icons on their profile too
• If your own copy of the game can't be read, your WFC trophies still show from the Store's list

WFC trophies + friends' levels ✿
• War for Cybertron now has trophies: all 50, read from your own copy of the game (icons included), with the ones you've already earned
• WFC counts towards your level and platinums, and shows in your trophy cabinet next to your Steam games
• New: show your level to friends. Open your profile and choose Share (Steam asks you to confirm it's you, Hanami never sees your password)
• Friends who share show their Hanami level in your friends list and on their profile, with their trophy counts and latest trophies
• See a friend's WFC trophies next to yours, with "You ✓" on the ones you both have
• Change your mind any time in Settings → Trophies: turning sharing off deletes your profile from the server

Friend profiles, PS5-style ✿
• Selecting a friend now opens their profile: status, what they're playing, Steam level and hours in the last 2 weeks
• Their recently played games, with hours, last played and trophy progress (Platinum shows when they've 100%'d it)
• Message, View trophies, Steam profile and Remove friend, right on their profile
• View trophies: see a friend's full trophy list for a game, with "You ✓" on the ones you've earned too
• Compare with your games: open any of your games to see how a friend is doing in it
• Back from a profile returns to your friends list
• In the friends list, F / Y still jumps straight to Message

- New: your Hanami profile ✿ Click your name in the top bar
- Trophies from your Steam achievements: rarer = better (bronze, silver, gold), and 100% of a game earns a platinum
- A PS5-style level, recently earned trophies, and a trophy cabinet with every game's progress
- Pick a game in the cabinet to see all its trophies, how rare they are and when you earned them

- Welcome to the Hanami beta ✿
- Settings → Send feedback (also in the M menu): saves a report with Hanami's logs to your Downloads, with logins and keys blanked out
- Hanami now keeps its own log, so problems can actually be tracked down

- War for Cybertron has its real key art in the Store, and on its tile in Games and Library
- Store card text stays readable on bright artwork

- Smoother home screen: moving between games no longer stutters (Hanami's work per frame cut by more than half)
- Petals fall at a silky 60 fps
- Patch notes now pop up right here on the home screen after an update, with Don't show again
- Settings → Show patch notes after updates turns the popup back on

- When a new Hanami comes out while it's open, the home screen shows it: F2 to update!
- After updating, the patch notes open in a new What's new tab
- Settings → Patch notes shows every version's notes
- The in-game menu's button row is back, with Close game: press it twice to quit and return to Hanami's home screen

- Fixed: your controller could steer Hanami (and launch games) while you played a game in front of it
- Notifications that pop up during a game no longer take button presses
- On laptops with two graphics chips, Store games now run on the fast one (NVIDIA/AMD)

- Hanami goes to sleep while you play, so games get the whole GPU
- Home screen and Control Center are much lighter, with the same look
- New: Settings → Lighter effects, for older graphics cards
- WFC updates keep the gamertag you set in the game

- Updates now install right inside Hanami — no extra windows
- If an update ever can't start, Hanami goes back to the version that works
- Recomp updates show a big progress popup with what's new

- Hanami updates itself from GitHub when it opens
- Recomps update from the Store, with progress in Downloads
